rules: INSPIRE is an open-source dataset developed for the INSPIRE Directive.
INSPIRE covers locations of freehold registered property in England and Wales.
INSPIRE is a subset of HM Land Registry Index Polygons for freehold land and property.
INSPIRE files are divided by local-authority area.
A polygon crossing a local-authority boundary can appear in both local-authority files.
INSPIRE polygons show position and indicative extent of registered property.
Each INSPIRE polygon has a unique Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
A Land Registry-INSPIRE ID relates to a registered title.
Find a Property can use an INSPIRE ID to obtain title registration and plan.
INSPIRE polygons cannot establish the definitive extent of a registered title.
Definitive registered-title extent requires inspection of the individual title plan.
Each registered title has one title number.
One registered title can contain several separate INSPIRE polygons.
Each separate INSPIRE polygon has its own INSPIRE ID.
Absence of an INSPIRE ID can mean land is not registered.
Absence of an INSPIRE ID can also reflect leasehold or another tenure excluded from INSPIRE.
Search the index map is the HMLR route for checking whether land is registered.
MapSearch exposes the full Index Polygon dataset to business e-services customers.
INSPIRE data and attributes are reusable under the Open Government Licence.
OGL reuse of INSPIRE data is free.
Failure to comply with OGL conditions ends the granted reuse rights automatically.
INSPIRE reuse requires HM Land Registry attribution.
Reuse of polygon geometry also requires Ordnance Survey attribution.
The current OS geometry attribution identifier is AC0000851063.
Where possible, INSPIRE reuse should link to the published conditions of use.
INSPIRE is updated on the first Sunday of each month.
An INSPIRE monthly release represents data from the previous month.
A monthly INSPIRE release remains accessible until the next release.
INSPIRE files are published in GML format.
A GIS is needed to view downloaded INSPIRE polygons.
GIS software can store or edit downloaded INSPIRE polygon data.
GIS software can compare INSPIRE data with other datasets.
GIS software can integrate INSPIRE data with other datasets.
HMLR uses GML as an open data format.
HMLR GML is intended to provide a standard structure across GIS and CAD systems.
GML can be converted into other GIS formats.
Using GML in another tool may require projection conversion.
QGIS is identified by HMLR as free open-source software for viewing and converting GML.
HMLR GML can be converted to ESRI Shapefile.
HMLR GML can be converted to MapInfo MIF or TAB.
HMLR GML can be converted to AutoCAD DXF.
HMLR GML can be converted to GeoJSON.
HMLR GML can be converted to KML.
HMLR polygon coordinates are captured against British National Grid.
HMLR warns BNG-to-WGS84 reprojection can shift some features by up to 15 metres.
Planning Data provides more than 100 planning and housing datasets through one interface.
A coordinate query uses latitude and longitude to construct a point for spatial intersection.
Longitude requires latitude in an entity search.
Latitude requires longitude in an entity search.
A coordinate query can request multiple datasets in one call.
Multiple dataset parameters return matches from any selected dataset.
Planning Data recommends UPRN queries as more precise than coordinates for registered properties.
The q parameter can search by postcode.
The q parameter can search by UPRN.
Entity results can include name.
Entity results can include dataset.
Entity results can include start-date.
Entity results can include geometry as WKT.
Entity results can include point as WKT.
Absence of Planning Data results does not prove that no planning constraint exists.
Planning Data coverage can vary by area.
Planning Data documents 337 local planning authorities in its all-LPA example.
Raw geometry queries accept WKT.
WKT geometry coordinates should use WGS84 EPSG:4326.
Spaces in WKT query strings must be percent-encoded.
The geometry_relation value can be within.
The geometry_relation value can be equals.
The geometry_relation value can be disjoint.
The geometry_relation value can be intersects.
The geometry_relation value can be touches.
The geometry_relation value can be contains.
The geometry_relation value can be covers.
The geometry_relation value can be coveredby.
The geometry_relation value can be overlaps.
The geometry_relation value can be crosses.
Large result sets can be paged with offset.
Planning Data recommends incrementing offset by the limit value.
Responses can include a pre-built next pagination link.
Responses can include a pre-built previous pagination link.
Responses can include a pre-built first-page link.
Responses can include a pre-built last-page link.
The portfolio-screening API has no batch endpoint.
API portfolio screening uses one request per property.
The field parameter can limit returned attributes.
Planning Data recommends polite rate-limiting between per-property requests.
For hundreds of properties or more, Planning Data recommends bulk downloads.
Large portfolios can be screened by local spatial intersection against bulk data.
Bulk downloads provide a stable snapshot for portfolio processing.
Bulk downloads can be available as CSV.
Bulk downloads can be available as JSON.
Bulk downloads can be available as GeoJSON.
Bulk downloads can be available as Parquet.
Planning Data describes Parquet as well suited to large datasets.
The API remains beta and may change for production users.
The entity endpoint extension must be json, html or geojson.
The current LIDAR Composite DTM 1m covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The current LIDAR Composite DTM 1m has 1 metre spatial resolution.
The DTM 1m is produced from the last or only laser pulse return.
DTM production removes surface objects from the DSM.
DTM surface-object removal uses bespoke algorithms.
DTM surface-object removal also uses manual editing.
The DTM 1m was produced by the Environment Agency in 2022.
The DTM 1m combines Time Stamped archive surveys with National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where surveys repeat, the newest and best-resolution source is selected for the composite.
Where source data is resampled, bilinear interpolation is used before merging.
The 2022 DTM 1m composite includes surveys from 6 June 2000.
The 2022 DTM 1m composite includes surveys through 2 April 2022.
Survey index catalogues identify which source survey was used at a location.
DTM 1m is downloadable as GeoTIFF raster data.
DTM 1m is distributed in 5 kilometre tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
DTM 1m elevations are expressed in metres.
DTM 1m elevations are referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
DTM 1m uses the OSTN15 transformation method.
Individual LIDAR surveys contributing to the composite have documented vertical accuracy of ±15 cm RMSE.
DTM 1m is licensed under the Open Government Licence.
DTM 1m declares annual update frequency.
DTM 1m uses EPSG:27700.
DTM 1m metadata extent begins at latitude 49.943.
DTM 1m metadata extent reaches latitude 55.816.
DTM 1m metadata extent begins at longitude -6.236.
DTM 1m metadata extent reaches longitude 2.072.
DTM 1m metadata identifier is 13787b9a-26a4-4775-8523-806d13af58fc.
DTM 1m exposes a WMS service.
DTM 1m exposes a WCS service.
DTM 1m exposes a WMTS service.
DTM 1m exposes an OGC API Features service.
The LIDAR Composite DTM 2m covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The LIDAR Composite DTM 2m has 2 metre spatial resolution.
DTM 2m uses the same last-or-only-return terrain-production concept.
DTM 2m is derived from Time Stamped and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
DTM 2m uses newest, best-resolution data where repeat surveys exist.
DTM 2m uses bilinear interpolation where resampling is required.
DTM 2m metadata identifier is 09ea3b37-df3a-4e8b-ac69-fb0842227b04.
DTM 2m exposes WMS, WCS and WMTS services.
DTM 2m exposes an OGC API Features service.
The LIDAR Composite DSM 1m covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The DSM 1m has 1 metre spatial resolution.
DSM 1m is produced from the last or only laser pulse return.
DSM 1m retains surface objects such as vehicles, buildings and vegetation.
DSM 1m combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
DSM 1m uses newest, best-resolution data where repeat surveys exist.
DSM 1m uses bilinear interpolation where source resampling is required.
DSM 1m is supplied as GeoTIFF rasters in 5 kilometre tiles.
The LIDAR Composite DSM 2m covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The DSM 2m has 2 metre spatial resolution.
DSM 2m retains vehicles, buildings and vegetation as well as terrain.
DSM 2m metadata identifier is f083c5dc-504f-4428-9811-a1b2519fa279.
DSM 2m uses EPSG:27700.
DSM 2m exposes WMS, WCS and WMTS services.
DSM 2m exposes an OGC API Features service.
The First Return DSM 1m covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The First Return DSM 1m uses the first or only laser return.
First Return DSM 1m can retain vehicles, buildings and vegetation.
First Return DSM 1m uses National LIDAR Programme data captured from 11 November 2016.
First Return DSM 1m source capture extends through 5 May 2022.
The National LIDAR Programme divided England into roughly 300 survey blocks.
Those survey blocks were captured over continuous winters from 2016 onwards.
First Return composite surveys are merged with feathering along overlaps.
Feathering is used to reduce small elevation differences between overlapping surveys.
First Return DSM 1m is supplied as 5 kilometre GeoTIFF tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
First Return DSM 1m exposes WMS, WCS and WMTS services.
First Return DSM 1m exposes an OGC API Features service.
The First Return DSM 2m has 2 metre spatial resolution.
First Return DSM 2m uses the same 11 November 2016 to 5 May 2022 source period.
DTM 10m is resampled from the LIDAR Composite DTM 2m.
DTM 10m resampling uses bilinear interpolation.
DTM 10m is a terrain model with surface objects removed.
DTM 10m is available as a single GeoTIFF raster aligned to the OS National Grid.
DTM 10m elevations are in metres referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
DTM 10m uses OSTN15.
DTM 10m is licensed under the Open Government Licence.
DTM 10m has annual update frequency.
DTM 10m metadata identifier is ce8fe7e7-bed0-4889-8825-19b042e128d2.
DTM 10m has no web data services listed on its dataset record.
The retired 25 cm composite DTM has been replaced by the 1 m composite product.
OS Terrain 50 is an open height dataset for Great Britain.
OS Terrain 50 represents a digital terrain model with protruding features removed from bare earth.
OS Terrain 50 is updated annually in July.
OS Terrain 50 is published as grid data.
OS Terrain 50 is published as contour data.
Grid and contour products are created from the same source data.
Grid and contour data are supplied as 10 km by 10 km tiles.
Terrain 50 tiles are identified by the National Grid reference of the southwest corner.
The Terrain 50 grid uses regular 50 metre post spacing.
Terrain 50 contour data uses standard 10 metre contour intervals.
Terrain 50 contour data includes mean high water boundaries.
Terrain 50 contour data includes mean low water boundaries.
Terrain 50 coverage is Great Britain.
Terrain 50 has a nominal scale of 1:50,000.
Terrain 50 grid data is available in ASCII format.
Terrain 50 grid data is available in GML 3.2.1 Simple Features Profile level 0.
Terrain 50 contours are available in GML 3.2.1 Simple Features Profile level 0.
Terrain 50 contours are available in Esri Shapefile.
Terrain 50 contours are available in GeoPackage.
Terrain 50 contours are available as vector tiles in MBTiles.
Terrain 50 is free to view as OpenData.
Terrain 50 is free to download as OpenData.
Terrain 50 is free to use for commercial purposes.
Terrain 50 is free to use for educational purposes.
Terrain 50 is free to use for personal purposes.
Terrain 50 online download requires no registration.
The tiled national supply contains 2,858 10 km tiles.
The 2,858 tiles are arranged into 55 folders.
Each tiled folder represents a 100 km National Grid square.
GeoPackage supply is a single national flat file.
Vector-tile supply is a single national flat file.
Grid and contour tiled supplies are delivered separately.
Terrain 50 tiled supply uses ZIP compression.
Terrain 50 ZIP data is not encrypted.
Contour compression rates vary with feature density in the geographic area.
A full national Terrain 50 grid supply is approximately 157 MB compressed.
Terrain 50 annual updates are delivered by full tile resupply.
Terrain 50 source data comes from the large-scale revision programme used for OS MasterMap Topography Layer.
The source DTM is captured as a triangulated irregular network.
The source TIN is edited using mass points and breaklines and/or automated techniques.
A TIN retains feature edges more accurately than a regular grid for source modelling.
Both grid and contour Terrain 50 products are interpolated from the source TIN.
ASCII Terrain 50 is a text-based raster-grid format.
ASCII Terrain 50 can be read by most standard GIS software without additional translation.
The Terrain 50 ASCII supply includes companion GML metadata.
Companion grid GML carries location information.
Companion grid GML carries grid-spacing information.
Companion grid GML carries vertical-reference information.
Terrain 50 ASCII rows run west to east.
Each Terrain 50 ASCII row contains 200 pixels.
Each Terrain 50 ASCII pixel represents 50 metres by 50 metres.
The OS Downloads API OpenData endpoints do not require an API key.
OS Downloads API OpenData downloads can be filtered by area.
The documented OpenData area enumeration includes TQ.
An OpenData download request can return HTTP 307 when redirect is requested and exactly one file matches.

blocked_gates.rule: Current July 2026 Barnet/Enfield entries are indexed, but exact public GML href bytes, downloaded bytes and SHA-256 remain unread because direct transport still loops or is not exposed.
Three candidate-specific valid Land Registry-INSPIRE IDs with exact native-British-National-Grid containment remain unresolved.
Exact coordinate responses for the three candidates remain unread because parameterized candidate URLs are blocked by execution URL safety.
Exact reference-filter responses for parcel refs 52040420, 52213916 and 52213412 remain uncaptured; search-index absence is not NO_DATA.
Exact TQ2892 filtered survey-feature metadata remains unread despite official DTM/DSM service contracts being known.
Exact candidate WCS GetCoverage GeoTIFF bytes, NoData evaluation, SHA-256 and numeric elevations remain absent.
Terrain50 productId is strongly supported by a direct OS API link, but official OS product-details JSON readback remains absent.
Actual current Terrain50 TQ29 binary bytes, SHA-256 and row149 col173/174 height cells remain absent.
F-host guarded recovery and runtime outputs HD2 015 plus HD1 016/025/identity-provenance runtime remain absent; no second runner is allowed.
